Minnetonka Stop at Six is a resident-led committee working to establish a 6% cap on annual increases in the City of Minnetonka's property tax levy.
Our goal is to help keep Minnetonka a great, affordable place to live through a budget initiative focused on the cap.

# The Proposal

Your property tax bill shouldn't be a surprise every year. 
We're working to cap annual property tax levy increases at 6%, so Minnetonka stays affordable for the people who call it home.
The property tax levy has nearly doubled over the last ten years.
Has your income doubled?

Minnetonka works because of its people: families who've been here for generations, seniors who want to stay in the homes they've paid off, young families buying their first house, and small businesses on our corners.

When property taxes go up faster than paychecks and retirement incomes, those same people get squeezed out. 
Stop at Six sets a clear, simple limit. 
However, the budget changes; the levy can't grow more than 6% in a year without a vote.

* **Predictable.** Households and businesses can plan ahead.
* **Fair.** Longtime residents and newcomers have the same protection.
* **Accountable.** City leaders still have room to invest. They just must set priorities within a reasonable limit.

Legally, the Minnetonka Stop at Six proposal is a Minnetonka Charter Budget Amendment.
It limits annual property tax levy increases to 6% - unless there is an approval vote from the residents.

You can find the current _draft_ proposal language [here](./files/stop-at-six-5.21-v3-charter-amendment.pdf){target="_blank"}

# The Process

In order to get the proposal enacted requires a majority vote via a ballot initiative.
The first step to getting an initiative on the ballot is to gather signatures.
This is where we are at.
The number of signatures is based on how many people voted in the Nov 3rd 2026 election.
The plan is to have the initiative voted on in Nov 2027.
This would mean that the property tax levy set in Dec 2028 (for tax year 2029) would be the first one implemented under the cap.
This allows for the elevated property tax levy's based on the current Public Safety Plan to be complete and Minnetonka returns to "normal".
In the future, the city would have an extra two percent plus to better Minnetonka on top of the normal cost of living.

# Historical Levy Rates

```{r}
#| label: fig-taxrates
#| fig-cap: "Source: MN DOR (actual), City of Minnetonka (future)"
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2)
taxdata <- tibble::tribble(
  ~years, ~rates, ~safety, ~future,
  2006, 9.8, F, F,
  2007, 9.3, F, F,
  2008, 4.7, F, F,
  2009, 5.7, F, F,
  2010, 2.0, F, F,
  2011, 2.9, F, F,
  2012, 0.9, F, F,
  2013, 1.5, F, F,
  2014, 2.8, F, F,
  2015, 2.9, F, F,
  2016, 4.0, F, F,
  2017, 5.0, F, F,
  2018, 3.6, F, F,
  2019, 3.8, F, F,
  2020, 6.9, F, F,
  2021, 3.5, F, F,
  2022, 5.6, F, F,
  2023, 6.4, F, F,
  2024, 7.5, T, F,
  2025, 7.3, T, F,
  2026, 7.9, T, F,
  2027, 6.4, T, F,
  2028, 7.4, T, T,
  2029, 4.4, F, T
)
taxdata$years <- as.integer(taxdata$years)
ggplot(taxdata, aes(x=years, y=rates, fill=safety, color=future)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('grey50', 'blue')) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('grey50', 'red')) +
  geom_text(aes(label=format(rates, nsmall=1)), lineheight = 0.7, vjust = -0.2, color='black') + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 6, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") + 
  labs(title="Levies Total - Year-over-Year % Increase", x = "Year", y = "% Increase", fill = "Public Safety Year?", color = "Future Year?")
```

# What Can I Do?

There are lots of ways to support Minnetonka Stop at Six!

You can donate, volunteer for various tasks, gather signatures, organize a "town hall", or request to receive updates.
You can find an email form, donation information, and links to find out more on the [Resources & Contact page](./resources.html)
